user_message.content: How should the seat-back strength clauses in GB 15083-2019 be understood?

assistant_message.content:
Under GB 15083-2019, seat-back strength requirements cover two dimensions: (1) seat backs that form the front boundary of the luggage compartment must provide protective strength against luggage displacement injuring occupants (clause 4.11.1); and (2) the seat back and its adjustment devices must meet general static strength requirements (clause 5.2). Details:

**1. Luggage displacement protection (seats forming the luggage compartment boundary)**
*   **Core requirement**: With the seat in the normal use position, the seat back and/or head restraint forming the luggage compartment shall have sufficient strength to protect occupants from injury due to forward luggage movement in a frontal impact.
*   **Acceptance criteria**:
    *   During and after the dynamic test in Annex B, the seat back and its locking devices shall remain in their original position.
    *   Deformation is allowed, but the forward contour of parts with Shore A hardness greater than 50 (seat back or head restraint) shall not move forward of specified transverse vertical planes:
        *   Head restraint: a point 150 mm forward of the seat R-point.
        *   Seat back: a point 100 mm forward of the seat R-point.
    *   Measurement excludes the rebound phase of the test blocks; test blocks shall remain behind the seat back during the test.
*   **Test method (Annex B)**:
    *   **Load simulation**: Rigid test blocks simulate luggage. Type 1: 300 mm x 300 mm x 300 mm, 18 kg; Type 2: 500 mm x 350 mm x 125 mm, 10 kg.
    *   **Placement**: Place two Type 1 blocks on the luggage floor with the front face against the front boundary, then move rearward until the center of gravity displaces 200 mm horizontally (or as far as possible / adjust seats if space is insufficient).
    *   **Dynamic conditions**: Secure the body on a sled for deceleration or acceleration; velocity change 50 (+0/-2) km/h; deceleration/acceleration-time curve per Figure B.3.
    *   **Seat state**: Longitudinal adjuster fixed one notch or 10 mm forward of the rearmost use position; height-adjustable head restraint at the highest position.

**2. General static strength (clause 5.2)**
*   **Test method**: Using a simulated human backform, apply a 530 Nm moment rearward relative to the seat R-point to the upper seat-back frame.
*   **Acceptance criteria**: During or after the test, the seat frame, anchorages, adjustment devices, and locking devices shall not fail. Permanent deformation that does not increase injury severity is allowed, provided the prescribed load is sustained.
*   **Exemption**: If the seat or back does not fracture in the head-restraint strength test per 5.4.3.6, it is deemed to meet 5.2; otherwise a separate 5.2 test is required.

**3. Other related constraints**
*   **Locking devices**: Shall not release during the above tests.
*   **Energy absorption**: Seat-back parts in Zone 1 must also meet energy-absorption requirements (headform deceleration above 80 g lasting no more than 3 ms), except for the rearmost seats, back-to-back seats, or seats meeting GB 11552.

key_clauses.original_text: Annex B (Normative) Test method for luggage displacement occupant protection devices. B.1 Test blocks. B.1.1 General: rigid test blocks with center of inertia coincident with geometric center. B.1.2 Type 1: 300 mm x 300 mm x 300 mm; all edges rounded to 20 mm radius; mass 18 kg; moment of inertia (0.3 +/- 0.05) kg·m^2 about all three principal axes. B.1.3 Type 2: 500 mm x 350 mm x 125 mm; edges rounded 20 mm; mass 10 kg. B.2 Test preparation. B.2.1 Seat-back test (see Figure B.1). Parts with Shore A hardness less than 50 may be removed at the manufacturer's option. Place two Type 1 blocks on the luggage floor; first contact the front boundary, then move rearward until the center of gravity displaces 200 mm horizontally (or adjust seats / place as far rearward as possible). Distance from vehicle longitudinal center plane to the inner face of each block shall be 25 mm (50 mm between blocks). Longitudinal adjuster fixed one notch or 10 mm forward of the rearmost use position; height-adjustable head restraint at highest position. If Type 1 blocks cannot be placed behind the seat, the test is not required. B.2.2 Partition device test: Type 2 block on a raised platform with its center of gravity midway between the seat-back top (excluding head restraint) and the lower edge of the roof liner; also place two Type 1 blocks per B.2.1. B.3 Dynamic test: Secure the body on a sled without reinforcing the seat back/partition. After placing blocks per B.2.1 or B.2.2, decelerate or accelerate the body so the curve remains within Figure B.3; velocity change 50 (+0/-2) km/h (simulating frontal impact).

key_clauses.original_text: 4.11.1 Seat backs. When the seat is in the normal use position specified by the manufacturer, the seat back and/or head restraint forming the luggage compartment shall have sufficient strength to protect occupants from injury due to forward luggage movement in a frontal impact. During and after the test described in Annex B, if the seat back and its locking devices remain in their original position, the requirement is considered met. During the test, deformation of the seat back and its fasteners is allowed, provided that the forward contour of the tested back and/or head restraint parts (Shore A hardness greater than 50) does not move forward of a transverse vertical plane passing through: (a) for the head-restraint portion, a point 150 mm forward of the seat R-point; (b) for the seat-back portion, a point 100 mm forward of the seat R-point. The rebound phase of the test blocks is excluded. For integral head restraints, the boundary between head restraint and seat back is defined by a plane perpendicular to the reference line at 540 mm from the R-point. All measurements shall be taken in the longitudinal center plane of each seat or seating position forming the front boundary of the luggage compartment. During the Annex B test, the test blocks shall remain behind the tested seat back.
key_clauses.explanation: This item is source-matched original regulation text; confirm applicability against current project conditions.

key_clauses.original_text: 5.2 Strength test of the seat back and its adjustment devices. Using a simulated human backform as described in Annex A of GB 11551-2014, apply a load producing a 530 Nm moment relative to the seat R-point rearward along the longitudinal direction to the upper part of the seat-back frame. For bench seats, if the supporting frame is wholly or partly shared by more than one seating position (including the head-restraint portion), those seating positions shall be tested simultaneously.
key_clauses.explanation: This item is source-matched original regulation text; confirm applicability against current project conditions.

key_clauses.original_text: 4.2.5 During or after the tests specified in 5.2 and 5.3, the seat frame, seat anchorages, adjustment devices, displacement devices and their locking devices shall not fail. Permanent deformation (including cracks) that does not increase injury severity in a collision is allowed, provided the prescribed load can be sustained.

key_clauses.original_text: 4.10.4 If the seat or back does not fracture during or after the test specified in 5.4.3.6, the strength of the seat back and its locking devices is deemed to meet 5.2. Otherwise, it shall be demonstrated that the seat can meet the 5.2 test requirements.

key_clauses.original_text: 4.2.6 During the tests specified in 5.3 and Annex B clause B.2.1, locking devices shall not release.

key_clauses.original_text: 4.2.3 For seat-back parts within Zone 1 determined per 5.8.1, when subjected to the energy-absorption test in Annex A, the duration of headform deceleration greater than 80 g shall not exceed 3 ms. Dangerous sharp edges shall not appear during or after the test. This requirement does not apply to the rearmost seats, back-to-back seats, or seats meeting GB 11552.
